name: FL-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent running in a seat with no expert-rated competitiveness
model.rationale: The district's R+18 lean, Patronis's incumbency and overwhelming financial edge, and markets pricing the race near 95% Republican all point the same direction, with no polls or ratings suggesting movement toward Valimont. The forecast stays essentially at the fundamentals-implied margin.
model.watch: Any late independent polling showing Valimont within single digits, or a surge of outside spending on her behalf, would be the first sign this is closer than the structural numbers suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northwest Florida's Panhandle seat is among the most Republican districts in the country, with an R+18 partisan lean. Jimmy Patronis, the incumbent, is running for a full term after winning the special election, and he holds an enormous resource advantage: roughly $3.8 million raised and $2.1 million in outside support, against about $174,000 raised by Democrat Gay Valimont. No outside groups are spending against Patronis in any meaningful way.

No public general-election polls cover the race, and no expert raters list it as competitive. Prediction markets price Patronis around 95% to win. With the fundamentals, money, and market pricing all aligned, the race is rated Safe Republican, with only modest residual uncertainty from the absence of polling.
